content_voiceover: This figure ties together everything about ADAMTS13 into the actual pathogenesis of TTP, and it's essentially a must know diagram for boards. On the left, under normal flowing blood, VWF multimers are anchored to the vessel wall and platelets attach through GPIb, forming small platelet VWF aggregates. What happens next branches into two pathways depending on ADAMTS13. When ADAMTS13 is present and functional, it continuously cleaves the stretched VWF, limiting how large these platelet aggregates can grow, so platelets and VWF fragments are released back into circulation, this is normal hemostasis, a self limited, regulated process. But when ADAMTS13 is absent or severely deficient, whether from an inherited mutation as in congenital TTP or an autoantibody as in acquired immune TTP, there is nothing to cleave the VWF, so platelet VWF aggregation continues unchecked. The bottom right panel shows the result, massive, uncontrolled platelet rich thrombi building up on the vessel wall, which is exactly what causes the diffuse microvascular thrombosis of TTP, consuming platelets, causing mechanical hemolysis as red cells shear through the narrowed vessels, and producing ischemic organ injury in the brain, kidneys, heart, and elsewhere. This single figure explains why plasma exchange, which replaces functional ADAMTS13 and removes autoantibody, is the cornerstone emergency treatment for acquired TTP.
keypoints: ADAMTS13 present: cleaves stretched VWF, limits platelet aggregate size, normal hemostasis
ADAMTS13 absent (mutation or autoantibody): unchecked VWF-platelet aggregation
Result: diffuse microvascular platelet-VWF thrombi = TTP
Explains why plasma exchange (replace ADAMTS13, remove autoantibody) is first-line TTP therapy
keypoint_voiceover: This figure is the core pathogenesis diagram for TTP. With functional ADAMTS13, VWF gets cleaved as it stretches, capping platelet aggregate size, that's normal hemostasis. Without ADAMTS13, from either a genetic mutation or an autoantibody, VWF-platelet aggregation runs unchecked, building the diffuse microvascular thrombi that define TTP. This is exactly why plasma exchange, restoring ADAMTS13 and clearing the autoantibody, is emergency first-line therapy.
